title: Expiratory muscle strength training for therapy of oropharyngeal dysphagia in older persons
summary:
Swallowing problems are common in older people and can lead to lung infections, weight loss, and reduced quality of life.
In everyday practice, the treatment of swallowing problems is often not uniform, and for many therapeutic approaches standardized training programs are lacking.
Breathing and swallowing partly use the same muscle groups, so targeted training of the breathing muscles may also strengthen muscles involved in swallowing.
This study investigates whether a structured breathing muscle training can improve swallowing function in older adults with swallowing difficulties.
Participants are randomly assigned to either a training group using a resistance device or a comparison group using a device without additional resistance and perform daily breathing exercises at home for six weeks.
Swallowing function is assessed before and after the training period using a standardized examination. In addition, questionnaires on quality of life and swallowing symptoms are completed.
The aim of the study is to determine whether breathing muscle training leads to a measurable improvement in swallowing function.

interventions.name:
Intervention arm (EMST)
Participants receive expiratory muscle strength training using the EMST-150 device.

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
Presence of clinically relevant oropharyngeal dysphagia confirmed by flexible endoscopic evaluation of swallowing (FEES).
Exclusion criteria:
Acute unstable medical or neurological conditions.
Severe respiratory disease preventing safe expiratory muscle strength training.
Inability to cooperate despite adequate support.
Contraindications to intensive respiratory muscle training.
Participation in another interventional study affecting swallowing function.
